devin: heads up — after the scheduler autotune merge last night I'm seeing a huge tail jump on continuous-batcher nodes, 99.9p went from ~120ms to ~1.8s for a subset of requests :grimacing:

maria: which pool / model?

devin: hostpool=cb-eu-2, model=vicuna-13b-q4_0. Affected ~12% of requests. throughput steady, but tail spikes align with small microbatch sizes being admitted repeatedly.

sasha: can you paste the alert? last 24h perf graph?

devin: alert: ALERT_LATENCY_99_9 cb-eu-2 2212345600
log snippet:
```
2026-03-18T03:22:11Z  svc=request id=... latency=1832ms kernel=fallback kv_hit=false batch_sz=2
2026-03-18T03:22:12Z  svc=request id=... latency=1789ms kernel=fallback kv_hit=false batch_sz=1
2026-03-18T03:22:14Z  svc=request id=... latency=1905ms kernel=optimized kv_hit=true batch_sz=16
```

ryan: oncall-bot also triggered CPU steal alerts on the same hosts earlier (possible noisy tenant). oncall-bot: "host-cb-27 cpu_steal > 15% for 3m"

maria: interesting. does kernel selector flip when batch size is small? we had a regression where kernel-selector preferred a fused kernel only if batch_sz >= 8. autotune might be pushing admission to favor latency for small queues and ends up forcing kernel fallback.

tariq: I ran a quick profile on a repro pod. small batches hit path that does extra memcpy in kv lookup loop. sample:
```
# flame (top few):
copy_kv_entry  45%
kernel_switch_overhead  20%
vectorized_attn_fallback  15%
others  20%
```

maria: kv hit rates for those noisy requests?

devin: KV cache hit rate drops to 8-12% for the slow requests vs 60-70% normally. looks like eviction + tiny microbatches = thrash.

sasha: so two things colliding: autotune reduced microbatch holding time (good for median), noisy neighbor increased eviction pressure -> low kv_hit -> kernel fallback + memcpy overhead -> tail.

ryan: mitigation options? rollback autotune or raise min_batch_hold to keep batch_sz>=8? we can also pin kernel selector to prefer optimized kernel for a few hostpools.

maria: safe short-term: revert autotune flag on cb-eu-2 and bump admission min_batch=6 for that pool. also add a KV cache soft-reserve to avoid thrash.

tariq: I'll test pinning kernel selector on a canary host. quick patch:
```
// scheduler config override
pools.cb-eu-2.admission.min_batch_hold_ms = 12
pools.cb-eu-2.kernel_selector.override = "prefer_optimized"
```

devin: running canary now on host-cb-27 (rolling restart). watching p99/p99.9.

oncall-bot: deployment cb-eu-2/canary started at 2026-03-18T03:45:10Z

sasha: while canary runs, let's capture a short pprof and KV telemetry window 60s before/after. devin, can you run this query and paste results?
```
sum(rate(kv_lookup_total[1m])) by (host)
sum(rate(kv_lookup_miss[1m])) by (host)
histogram_quantile(0.999, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```

devin: pasted below:
- host-cb-27 kv_hit=14% -> p99.9=1.7s
- host-cb-28 kv_hit=68% -> p99.9=130ms

maria: canary results?

devin: canary shows 99.9p dropped back to 145ms on host-cb-27 after override. KV hit stabilized to ~55%.

ryan: ok rollback plan for prod: 1) set admission.min_batch_hold_ms=12 on cb-eu-2 2) add kernel_selector override for pool 3) gradual rollout 25/50/100% over 20m 4) monitor p99/p99.9 and kv_hit

sasha: follow-ups: open perf issue to remove memcpy in kv loop (tariq), add regression test that simulates eviction+tiny-batch workload (devex), and add an alert for kv_hit_rate drop under 20% for 5m (alerts).

maria: assigning tasks — tariq (PR for kv memcpy elimination), devex (synthetic regression harness), ryan (rollout), devin (postmortem draft).

devin: started rollout at 2026-03-18T04:05:00Z, will update in 10m. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: rollout step 1 -> 25% complete at 2026-03-18T04:15:43Z

devin: 10m update: p99.9 down to ~220ms cluster-wide, kv_hit increased to 48% on most hosts. still tracking two hosts with weird steal pattern.

maria: great. keeping this thread as the incident trail. we'll leave open until PRs and regression test merged.

ryan: filing incident ticket INF-2026-042 referencing this thread and the alert id.

devin: postmortem draft link: https://redwood-internal/pm/INF-2026-042/draft — comments welcome.

sasha: nice quick mitigation. long term we need more robust admission logic that considers kv pressure + kernel costs, not just queue latency.

maria: agreed. thanks everyone. :sparkles:
